title: Control Bar grouping
contract: The chapter groups Control Bar roles into nine named sections: Browser Options; Tempo Settings and Metronome; Scale Settings; Follow and Arrangement Position; Transport Controls; Automation and Capture MIDI; Arrangement Loop Settings; MIDI and CPU Settings; View Selector. This is a documentary grouping, not pixel/order/visibility geometry or a new definition of the domain controls.

title: Shared scale selection and future clips
contract: Control Bar scale controls reflect the selected clip and offer Scale Mode, Root Note and Scale Name. With no clip selected, chosen scale settings apply to subsequently created clips. This adds the global selection/default context to Clip View properties; accepted scale lists, data codec, preference scope and numerical pitch transforms remain with existing owners or unknown.

title: Scale controls with multiple clips
contract: Control Bar Scale controls can turn Scale Mode on/off or set the same scale for multiple selected clips. Mixed audio/MIDI selections, incompatible tuning, empty-slot versus existing-clip propagation and merge/display precedence remain unknown. This does not redefine perclip Scale or a device retuning law.

title: Status messages and update context
contract: Status Bar can display error information and available-release updates, the latter in the documented Automatic Updates enabled context. Error wording, severity, retention, availability checks, update protocol/consent and whether other notifications appear are unknown; delivery owns update operations.

title: Selected-note Status Bar details
contract: With a selected MIDI Note Editor note, Status Bar provides its location, pitch, velocity and probability details. Numeric encoding, pitch naming, formatting, rounding, multi-selection aggregation and update deadlines remain unknown; note values/editing remain MIDI-owner contracts.

title: Insert-marker hover feedback
contract: Hovering an actually offered insert marker in the documented Session/Arrangement context displays its location in Status Bar. Which Session/editor marker is intended, exact location grammar/precision, hidden-marker handling and focus/hover timing remain unknown; no marker coordinate formula is inferred.

title: Two-window view swap
contract: With two Live windows and Use Tab Key to Navigate disabled, Tab swaps Session and Arrangement between the windows. Existing keyboard-navigation owns the one-window Tab switch, preference-conditioned focus traversal and platform view shortcuts; this adds only the paired-window swap context.

title: View switching versus playing state
contract: The chapter describes Session/Arrangement view switching during playback/recording as a UI change that does not change the currently playing clips. It does not specify sample continuity, a no-glitch deadline, record event ordering or arbitrary UI-command independence; transport/launch/record owners retain those laws.

title: Track-title Device View entry
contract: Double-clicking a track title opens Device View for its device chain. This adds an entry gesture, not device insertion/classification/routing or clip/device stack behavior. Generic device focus remains with keyboard-navigation and stacking/Clip View selection with Clip View.

title: Scale propagation and folding contexts
contract: Global no-selection/future-clip/empty-slot propagation, mixed-selection state, Fold to Scale exceptions, scale-aware device/MIDI-tool conversion and tuning interactions remain unresolved beyond linked owners.

title: Status and control feedback limits
contract: Error/update, marker/note field grammar, multi-selection/hidden/focus contexts, warnings and inaccessible or unavailable controls have no complete feedback oracle.

title: Workspace layout and window outcomes
contract: Window creation/closure, selected-view conflicts, minimization, displays/scaling, unavailable shortcuts, focus restoration and layout persistence remain required unknowns.

title: Workspace failures and lifecycle
contract: Undo/redo/cancel, invalid/unsupported settings, object/media/device loss, audio-rate/engine/transport changes, concurrent controls and teardown remain unknown.
